materials.title: A call to Uncle Dan
materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Uncle Dan: Hello, Mia! Can you hear me?
Mia: ____

2. Uncle Dan: Who is sitting beside you?
Mia: ____

3. Mia: Please show me your new puppy.
Uncle Dan: ____

4. Uncle Dan: Pip is asleep. Please speak quietly.
Mia: ____

5. Mia: I must go to dinner now. Goodbye!
Uncle Dan: ____

questions.prompt:
Uncle Dan: Hello, Mia! Can you hear me?
Mia: ____
options: Yes. I can hear you now.
questions.explanation: The reply confirms hearing. Location, apple count and identity do not answer an audio check.

questions.prompt:
Uncle Dan: Who is sitting beside you?
Mia: ____
questions.explanation: Naming the brother identifies the person. Day, colour preference and ability do not.

questions.prompt:
Mia: Please show me your new puppy.
Uncle Dan: ____
options: Here he is. His name is Pip.
questions.explanation: Showing and naming the puppy responds to the request. Place/time/shoes do not show it.

questions.prompt:
Uncle Dan: Pip is asleep. Please speak quietly.
Mia: ____
options: All right. I will use a quiet voice.
questions.explanation: A promise to lower the voice follows the request. Unrelated sightings/objects do not.

questions.prompt:
Mia: I must go to dinner now. Goodbye!
Uncle Dan: ____
questions.explanation: The farewell and good wish close the call appropriately. Location/body/ability do not.

units.title: The empty seat
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The empty seat
materials.text:
Finn takes his lunch to a table in the school garden. There are three children there and one empty seat. "Can I sit here?" he asks.

"Yes," says Ada. She moves her bag from the seat to the ground. Finn sits down. He has rice and chicken. Ada has noodles in a blue box.

A little bird lands near the table. Finn watches it, but he does not give it his lunch. After eating, the children put their rubbish in the bin. Ada picks up her bag. The seat is empty again when they go back to class.

questions.prompt: Finn asks before sitting down.
questions.explanation: He asks Can I sit here?

questions.prompt: Ada’s bag is on the seat at first.
questions.explanation: She moves it from the seat to the ground.

questions.prompt: Finn has noodles in a blue box.
questions.explanation: Ada has noodles; Finn has rice and chicken.

questions.prompt: Finn gives his lunch to the bird.
questions.explanation: He watches without giving it his lunch.

questions.prompt: The children leave rubbish on the table.
questions.explanation: They put it in the bin.

units.title: Two clocks in the kitchen
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: Two clocks in the kitchen
materials.text:
Grandpa has two clocks in his kitchen. One is round and hangs above the door. The other is small and stands beside the bread bin. The round clock says eight o'clock, but the small one says seven.

"Which clock is right?" asks Lily.

Grandpa looks at his watch. It is eight. He puts a new battery in the small clock and moves its hands. Now both clocks show the same time.

Lily helps make breakfast. She puts two cups on the table. "We can have tea now," she says. Grandpa smiles. "Yes. Neither clock can make it for us!"

questions.prompt: There are two clocks in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: The opening gives two.

questions.prompt: The round clock stands beside the bread bin.
questions.explanation: The small clock stands there; the round one hangs above the door.

questions.prompt: Grandpa checks his watch.
questions.explanation: He uses it to find the correct time.

questions.prompt: The small clock gets a new battery.
questions.explanation: Grandpa puts one in it.

questions.prompt: Lily puts three cups on the table.
questions.explanation: She puts two cups there.

units.title: A ribbon on the bag
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: A ribbon on the bag
materials.text:
At the swimming pool, Hana sees three black bags beside the bench. Her bag is black too. She opens one and finds a large red towel. "This is not mine," she says. Her towel is yellow.

Mum helps her find the right bag. It is behind the bench, not beside the other three. Hana puts on her shoes and takes it home.

At home, she ties a green ribbon to the handle. The next Saturday, she sees the ribbon as soon as she comes out of the pool. She picks up her own bag and waits for Mum by the door.

questions.prompt: Hana’s bag is black.
questions.explanation: The story explicitly says her bag is black too.

questions.prompt: Her towel is red.
questions.explanation: Her towel is yellow; another bag contains red.

questions.prompt: Her bag is first found behind the bench.
questions.explanation: Mum helps find it there.

questions.prompt: Hana ties a ribbon to her shoes.
questions.explanation: She ties it to the bag handle.

questions.prompt: The ribbon helps her find the bag the next week.
questions.explanation: On the next Saturday she recognises it immediately.

units.title: The biscuit plate
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The biscuit plate
materials.text:
Sam puts six biscuits on a plate. He wants to share them with his two cousins. Before they arrive, he writes their names on three paper cups: Sam, Rose and Ben.

Rose comes first. She brings a bottle of juice. Ben comes with a small football. They all wash their hands, then sit at the table.

"Two biscuits each," says Sam. He puts two beside every cup. There are no biscuits left on the plate.

After their snack, Ben asks to play football. They take the ball to the garden. Rose leaves the juice bottle on the kitchen table, with its lid on.

questions.prompt: Sam puts six biscuits on a plate.
questions.explanation: Six is given in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: Rose and Ben are Sam’s cousins.
questions.explanation: They are the two cousins identified by cup names and arrivals.

questions.prompt: Rose brings a football.
questions.explanation: Rose brings juice; Ben brings the football.

questions.prompt: Each child has three biscuits.
questions.explanation: Each has two, using all six.

questions.prompt: They take the juice bottle into the garden.
questions.explanation: It stays on the kitchen table; they take the ball.

units.title: The puppet’s hat
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The puppet’s hat
materials.text:
Nina makes a paper puppet with Dad. It has a round face and a long blue coat. Nina draws black eyes and a small red mouth. Dad cuts out a yellow hat, but Nina does not glue it on.

"He may want a different hat tomorrow," she says. She puts the hat in a little envelope behind the puppet theatre.

In the evening, Nina gives a show for her brother. The puppet goes out in the rain. Nina takes the yellow hat from the envelope and puts it on his head. Her brother claps. "Now he can go to the shop!" he says.

questions.prompt: The puppet has a blue coat.
questions.explanation: Its coat is long and blue.

questions.prompt: Nina draws green eyes.
questions.explanation: She draws black eyes.

questions.prompt: The yellow hat is glued on at once.
questions.explanation: Nina deliberately leaves it separate.

questions.prompt: Nina keeps the hat in an envelope.
questions.explanation: It stays there behind the theatre.

questions.prompt: Nina puts the hat on during the show.
questions.explanation: She takes it out and puts it on the puppet’s head.
